Rashi on Shabbat 105b:10:1.english: You have counted my bemoaning [nodi] - [This is] an expression of “to bemoan [lanud] him” (Job 2[:11]).

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:10:2.english: And they buried him - It is written in Joshua.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:10:3.english: That the mountain raged against them to kill them - Because they did not eulogize [him] appropriately.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:10:4.hebrew: מדה כנגד מדה - הוא לא נתאבל על שנתקצרו ימי החכם, אף לחייו לא יחושו מן השמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:10:4.english: Measure for measure - He did not mourn that the Sage's days were cut short, [so] neither will Heaven be concerned for his life.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:11:1.english: Babylonian - For he came up [to the Land of Israel] from Babylonia.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:11:2.hebrew: ימים האריכו - שכלו ימיהם בטוב, דחשיב אריכות ימים, כדאמרי' בסדר יומא (דף עא.): "כי אורך ימים ושנות חיים יוסיפו" — וכי יש לך שנים של חיים ושנים שאינם של חיים? אמר רבי אלעזר: אלו שנותיו של אדם שמתהפכות עליו מרעה לטובה:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:11:2.english: They lengthened days - [Meaning] that they completed their days in goodness, which is considered length of days, as we say in Seder Yoma (71a): "For length of days and years of life they will add" — are there then years of life and years that are not of life? Rabbi Elazar said: These are a person's years that turn for him from bad to good.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:1:2.hebrew: כי כיסתא - התפירה הולכת ומתקפלת, שאין הבגד שוה ובולט בבגד כמין כיס. וצריך לקרוע הבגד למטה, ומולל לפניו, והתפירה מתיישבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:1:2.english: Like a pocket - [The seam] keeps folding up, because the garment is not even and it bulges out in the garment like a kind of pocket. And one must tear the garment below, and roll [the excess] in front of him, and [thus] the seam lies flat.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:2:1.hebrew: הסיט כפול - מפרש בגמרא: סיט הוא הפסק שבין אצבע לאמה, כמו שאדם יכול להרחיבו. ואם טוה וליבן וניפץ וצבע — שהן כולן אבות מלאכות — חוט א' ארוך כשיעור הזה, חייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:2:1.english: A double sit - [The Gemara] explains: a sit is the space between the index finger and the middle finger, as [wide as] a person can stretch it. And if one spun, whitened, combed, or dyed — all of which are primary labors — one thread as long as this measure, he is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:2:2.hebrew: האורג ב' חוטין שיעורו - ברוחב הבגד כמלא הסיט, שאע"פ שלא ארגו על פני כל רוחב הבגד, חייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:2:2.english: One who weaves two threads, his measure [is] - across the width of the garment, the full [width] of a sit; for even though he did not weave it across the entire width of the garment, he is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:3:1.hebrew: נראה בעיני דהכי <abbr title="גרסינן">גרסי'</abbr>: "ורמינהו הקורע בחמתו ובאבלו ועל מתו — חייב, <abbr title="ואף על פי">ואע"פ</abbr> כו'". ולמאי דגרס "הקורע בחמתו ובאבלו ועל מתו <abbr title="אף על פי">אע"פ</abbr> כו'" — לא ידענא מאי "יצא ידי הקריעה" שייך למימר אבחמתו, ואמאי נקט "בחמתו":
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:3:1.english: It appears to me that this is how we read [the text]: "And they raised a contradiction: One who rends [his garment] in his anger, or in his mourning, or over his dead [relative] is liable, and even though, etc." And according to the one who reads, "One who rends [his garment] in his anger, or in his mourning, or over his dead [relative], even though, etc." — I do not know how [the phrase] "he fulfilled [his obligation of] rending" is relevant to say regarding "in his anger," and why [the baraita] stated "in his anger."

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:3:2.english: He fulfilled his obligation of rending - for a person is obligated to rend [his garment] over his dead [relative].

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:3:3.hebrew: הא במת דידיה - ברייתא דקתני חייב, במת דידיה שחייב לקרוע עליו. הלכך, קריעה דידיה לאו קלקול הוא אלא תקון:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:3:3.english: This [refers] to his own dead [relative] - The baraita that teaches [that one is] liable [refers] to his own dead [relative], for whom he is obligated to rend [his garment]; therefore, his rending is not destruction, but rather repair.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:1.english: And "his dead" - is also taught in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:2.hebrew: לעול' במת דידיה - שמוטל עליו לקוברו, ומיהו בהנך דלאו בני אבלו' נינהו, שאינן מאותן האמורים בפרשת כהנים (ויקרא כא): אביו ואמו, בנו ובתו, ואחיו ואחותו:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:2.english: Actually, [it refers] to his [own] dead - [one] whom it is incumbent upon him to bury; however, [it refers] to those who are not subject to mourning, who are not among those stated in the section of the priests (Leviticus 21): his father and his mother, his son and his daughter, and his brother and his sister.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:3.hebrew: ופרכינן ואי חכם הוא - זה שמת, חיובי מיחייב נמי לקרוע, וכיון דמיחייב, מתקן הוא, ואמאי פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:3.english: And we ask: And if he is a scholar - [i.e.,] the one who died, [one] is also obligated to rend [one's garment], and since he is obligated, he is [performing a] constructive [act], so why is he exempt?

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:4.hebrew: חולצין - יוצאים לפניו חלוצי כתף, חלוקו קרוע עד שכתיפו חלוצה ערומה:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:4.english: [They] bare [their shoulders] - They go out before him with bared shoulder; his garment is torn until his shoulder is bared [and] exposed.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:5.hebrew: מברין עליו ברחבה - שהיו מברין האבלין ברחבה. סעודה ראשונה שאבל אוכל, אינו אוכל משלו ואסור, דקאמר ליה רחמנא ליחזקאל (כד), ״לחם אנשים לא תאכל״:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:4:5.english: Everyone eats the mourner’s meal over him in the public square - For they would serve the mourner’s meal to the mourners in the public square. [For] the first meal that a mourner eats, he does not eat of his own [food], and it is forbidden [for him to do so], as the Merciful One said to Ezekiel (24[:17]), "Do not eat the bread of [other] people."

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:5:1.english: Do they take security - Before he sins, did they take his pledge?

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:6:1.hebrew: לס"ת שנשרף - הרואה ס"ת שנשרף חייב לקרוע, כדאמרינן במו"ק (דף כו.) במגילה ששרף יהויקים, דכתיב "לא פחדו ולא קרעו בגדים". אף נשמת ישראל הניטלת דומה לו, שאין לך ריק בישראל שאין בו תורה ומצות:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:6:1.english: To a Torah scroll that was burned - One who sees a Torah scroll that was burned is obligated to rend [his garment], as we say in Moed Katan (26a) regarding the scroll that Yehoiakim burned, as it is written: "They were not afraid, nor did they rend [their] garments." So too, the soul of a Jew that is taken away is similar to it, for there is no empty [person] in Israel who does not have Torah and mitzvot.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:7:1.hebrew: הא ר' יהודה כו' - ומתו אמתו הכי נמי הוה מצי לתרוצי, אלא מעיקרא אהדר לאוקמינהו כחד תנא, ולא מתוקמא אלא כר' יהודה, דהא מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה היא, כמוציא את המת לקוברו:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:7:1.english: This [follows] Rabbi Yehuda, etc. - And [the contradiction between] "his dead [relative]" and "his dead [relative]" could also have been resolved in this way; however, initially [the Gemara] sought to establish them according to a single Tanna, and [together] they could only be established according to Rabbi Yehuda, for this is a labor not needed for its own sake, like one who carries out a corpse to bury it.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:8:1.english: Satisfaction for his inclination - For he calms his anger.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:8:2.hebrew: מי שרי והא תניא כו' - אלמא לאו מתקן הוא, שמלמד ומרגיל את יצרו לבא עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:8:2.english: Is it permitted? Wasn't it taught, etc. - Evidently, it is not [considered] constructive, for he teaches and accustoms his [evil] inclination to come upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:8:3.hebrew: בך - משמע בקרבך, שאם היה בך, תשתחוה לאל נכר לבסוף:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:8:3.english: Within you - [This] implies within your midst, for if it is within you, you will bow to a foreign god in the end.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:9:1.hebrew: שליף מצבייתא - מן הבגד בחמתו, להראותם שהוא כועס ויגורו מלפניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 105b:9:1.english: Pulled threads - From the garment in his anger, to show them that he is angry and they will fear him.

Rashi on Shabbat 105b:9:3.english: Niktema - The lid of the jug.

Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:10:1.hebrew: שרגש עליהן ההר כו' - משום דלא אשכחן דכתיב ביה "ויבכו אותו שלשים יום", כמו במשה ואהרן. ע"כ תוספות שאנץ. רש"ל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:10:1.english: "That the mountain raged against them, etc." - [They knew that they were lazy in eulogizing him] because we do not find that it is written regarding him [Joshua], "and they wept for him thirty days," as [is written] regarding Moses and Aaron. Thus far [is from] Tosafot Shantz. Rashal.

Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:4:1.hebrew: הכל חולצין עליו - אומר רשב"א דאפי' אינו רבו חייב, כדאמרינן במו"ק (דף כה.): "מי תני רבו שמת? חכם שמת תני!". והא דאמר בשילהי פרק אלו מציאות (ב"מ לג.): רבא קרע עליה דההוא גברא דאסבריה "זוהמא ליסטרון" — היינו קרע שאינו מתאחה, כדין תלמיד לרב, כדתני בפרק אלו מגלחין (מו"ק דף כו.):
Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:4:1.english: Everyone bares [his shoulder] over him - Rashba says that even if he is not his teacher, one is obligated [to rend his garment], as we say in Moed Katan (25a): "Did it teach 'his teacher who died'? It taught 'a scholar who died'!" And [as for] that which it says at the end of the chapter [entitled] Eilu Metziot (Bava Metzia 33a), [that] Rava tore [his garment] over that man who explained to him [the meaning of] zohama listron — that was a tear that may never be mended, in accordance with the law of a student for a teacher, as is taught in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Megalchin (Moed Katan 26a).

Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:6:1.hebrew: דתניא ר"ש בן אלעזר אומר העומד על המת כו' - משמע ליה להש"ס דמיירי אפי' באינו כשר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:6:1.english: "As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: One who is standing over the deceased, etc." - It is implied to the Gemara that [the baraita] refers even to one who is not worthy:

Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:7:1.hebrew: הא ר' יהודה והא ר"ש - פי' בקונט' דבהאי שינויא נמי משני דלא קשה מתו אמתו, והא דלא קאמר אלא משום דלא הוזכר אמורא לעיל. וקשה לר"י, דע"כ תרוייהו במת דידיה איירי, ולא במת דעלמא, כדקתני בברייתא דלעיל דיצא ידי קריעה; וא"כ, הויא מלאכה שצריכה לגופה, כיון שהיא צורך מצוה, כדמוכח לקמן. ונראה לר"י דלא מתרץ אלא חמתו אחמתו, אבל בעל מתו לא פליגי; דבמת דעלמא פטור דמקלקל הוא, ובמת דידיה דאיכא מצוה חשיב מתקן. אע"ג דלקמן משמע דלצורך מצוה לא חשיב ר"ש תיקון, דהא יליף ממילה והבערת בת כהן דמקלקל בחבורה ובהבערה חייב — התם מקלקל הוא לגמרי, שאינו צורך אחר אלא מה שהוא צורך מצוה; אבל גבי קריעת אבל, הוי תיקון הבגד על ידי קריעה, שיוכל ללובשו בכל שעה ואית בו חימום. ועוד, כמו שמחלק לקמן ר"ת: דהתם התיקון בא לבסוף, שבשעת חבורה והבערה אינה באה הכשר מצוה עד הגמר; אבל הכא, בשעת קריעה בא התיקון, ולא חשיב קלקול:
Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:7:1.english: This [ruling is] R. Yehuda, and that [ruling is] R. Shimon - Rashi explained that with this answer [the Gemara] also resolves [the contradiction so] that [the ruling regarding] his dead [relative] does not contradict [the other ruling regarding] his dead [relative], and the reason it did not say [this earlier] is only because no Amora had been mentioned above. And Ri finds this difficult: for perforce both [the Mishnah and the baraita] are speaking of his own dead [relative], and not of just any dead person, as the baraita above teaches that he has fulfilled the obligation of rending; and if so, it is a labor needed for its own sake, since it is for the sake of a mitzvah, as is proven below. Rather, it appears to Ri that [the Gemara] is only resolving [the contradiction between] "his anger" and "his anger," whereas regarding "for his dead [relative]" they do not disagree; for with just any dead person he is exempt because he is destructive, whereas with his own dead [relative], where there is a mitzvah, he is considered constructive. Even though below it is implied that R. Shimon does not consider [an act done] for the sake of a mitzvah to be constructive — for he derives from circumcision and the burning of a priest's daughter that one who is destructive through wounding or burning is liable — there it is completely destructive, as there is no other need besides what is for the sake of the mitzvah; whereas regarding the rending of a mourner, there is a repair to the garment through the rending, so that he can wear it at any time and there is warmth in it. Furthermore, [it can be answered] as Rabbeinu Tam distinguishes below: there, the repair comes at the end, for at the moment of wounding or burning the preparation of the mitzvah does not come until the completion; whereas here, at the moment of rending the repair comes [immediately], and it is not considered destruction.

Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:9:1.hebrew: לא צריכא דקעבד למירמא אימתא כו' - השתא הוה מצי לאוקמי תרווייהו כר' יהודה, ומתני' דלא עבד למירמא אימתא, דבלא"ה מוקמינן לקמן כר' יהודה דאמר מקלקל בחבורה פטור; אלא דניחא ליה לאוקמי מתני' בדעביד למירמא אימתא, דאי בחמתו — פשיטא דפטור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 105b:9:1.english: "It is only necessary [where] he acts to instill fear," etc. - Now, [the Gemara] could have established both of them in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and [explained] the Mishnah [as referring to a case] where he did not act to instill fear — for in any case we establish [the Mishnah] later in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says that one who causes damage by wounding is exempt; rather, it preferred to establish the Mishnah [as referring to a case] where he acts to instill fear, for if [he acted] in his anger, it is obvious that he is exempt.
